csv_project_name: Design Build for UIC Drug Discovery and Innovation Pavilion
csv_agency: State of Illinois Capital Development Board (CDB)
csv_scope_of_work: The University of Illinois Cancer Center, the University of Illinois (UIC) College of Pharmacy, the Discovery Partners Institute, and the State of Illinois are partnering to construct the 190,000 square-foot Drug Discovery and Cancer Research Pavilion (DDCRP), a new state-of-the-art facility to house emerging areas of translational research. This public-private partnership will bring together industry and university partners, educational and clinical programs, research, and our community to create a collaborative environment to drive therapeutic discovery. Located on UIC s West Campus, the DDCRP will be a 190,000 square-foot facility dedicated to cancer and pharmaceutical research with a focus on drug development and discovery. Several floors dedicated to cancer research, clinical oncology trials, and community outreach will extend the Cancer Center s capabilities as a convener of cutting-edge scientists and innovators. The College of Pharmacy and its investigational pharmacists are established leaders in drug development and translational oncology.
csv_disciplines_requested: Architecture Services, Design Build/Developer, Interior Design/Space Planning, Landscape Architecture, Programming, Civil Engineering

services: Design-build services with requested disciplines including architecture, interior design/space planning, landscape architecture, programming, civil engineering, and developer services.
relevance_explanation:
- Large and technically demanding university research building with 190,000 square feet.
- University and research campus projects are strategically relevant for sbp, especially large public institutional buildings.
- Early entry via design-build team formation can create opportunities for structural concept input.
- Likely complex laboratory/research building structure, but no explicit long-span, special roof, bridge, or signature structural system is described.
- Tender is broad design-build procurement rather than specifically structural engineering, which limits direct fit.
